## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Zá Āpítán Xīn Lùn* 雜阿毘曇心論 (Skt. *Saṃyuktābhidharma-hṛdaya-śāstra*, CBETA T28n1552) is a Liu Song (劉宋) dynasty translation of the third and most elaborated text in the *Hṛdaya* tradition, 11 juan, attributed to Dharmatrāta 尊者法救 ([法救](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E6%95%91)) and translated by Saṃghavarman 僧伽跋摩 ([僧伽跋摩](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E4%BC%BD%E8%B7%8B%E6%91%A9)) and others. The colophon identifies it as 宋天竺三藏僧伽跋摩等譯. The Taisho header "No. 1552 [cf. Nos. 1550, 1551]" marks its position in the *Hṛdaya* sequence.

**Abstract**

The *Saṃyuktābhidharma-hṛdaya* ("Mixed Heart of the Abhidharma") is attributed to Dharmatrāta 法救 (*Dharmatrāta*), a prominent Sarvāstivāda master of the Kaśmīra Vaibhāṣika tradition, also cited in the *Mahāvibhāṣā* as one of the four major masters whose views it presents. Frauwallner (1995) identifies the *Saṃyuktābhidharma-hṛdaya* as the most comprehensive text of the *Hṛdaya* tradition, substantially expanding on Dharmaśreṣṭhin's base text with the addition of "mixed" (*saṃyukta*) material from related Abhidharma sources.

The translator Saṃghavarman 僧伽跋摩 (*Saṃghavarman*, "Protected by the Saṃgha") was a Central Indian (*Tiānzhú* 天竺) monk who worked in the Liu Song court, translating several texts including this one. He was active in the mid-5th century CE.

The *Saṃyuktābhidharma-hṛdaya* was an important study text in Chinese Abhidharma circles. Together with T1550 and T1551, it forms a progressive trilogy of increasingly elaborated presentations of the Sarvāstivāda doctrinal system in summary format. Vasubandhu's *Abhidharmakośa* ([KR6l0023](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6l/KR6l0023)) may have been composed partly in response to and in dialogue with this tradition.
